answer: One operator minted many cheap farm badges and cashed seats as if each badge were an independent grower. Every rater now claims a single irrigation sluice under a marked cedar in a public grove, seats one crystal float only that sluice key can raise, and files six flow-staff readings 19 minutes apart at three gauge houses. Raising the float locks 5.1 stake-units for 33 hours. Auditors match those readings to gauge-house logs and cut any sluice whose crystal float or cedar mark appears on two ledgers. Two names on one grove sluice, or a reading that reuses a parent hash, forfeits the stake.
